ut_highway_wall.blurb: Highway Wall is a drytooling cliff in Provo Canyon, sitting at the far right end of the second tier above the Stairway to Heaven ice line. Its 16 mixed routes are bare-rock tool climbs rather than ice, with most falling between M5 and M8 and a single M4 and a single M9 at the ends. Harder lines favour thin, vertical movement on small holds, onsights can be tricky, and the topouts are spirited. To get there you either climb the first pitch of Stairway or walk a gully to the right and traverse back left above the lower cliff band.

ut_iron_hayden_wall.blurb: Iron Hayden Wall is a tall multi-pitch face in the middle of Hayden Peak's west side in the Uinta Mountains, at roughly 11,000 feet. It holds 16 alpine-style climbs, mostly trad with a few sport lines, from a handful of easy-to-moderate pitches up to 5.11, with the bulk at 5.10 and 5.11. The wall is exposed and can run cold and windy, so dress for it. It sits in shade through the morning and picks up sun later in the day. Bring a rack, since pure bolted lines are scarce.
ut_iron_hayden_wall.approach: From the Highline Trailhead, follow a trail through forest and up a gully, cross a talus field, then branch north on a cairned path to the base. The turn-off can be hidden in brush at a small creek crossing.

ut_red_rock_the.blurb: The Red Rock is a small crag in Draper, Utah, reached by a short trail from the trailhead. Sixteen routes are recorded: thirteen are bolted and three are trad, with a few that are commonly top-roped. Grades run from about 5.5 up to a lone 5.11, and the bulk sits between 5.6 and 5.10, which makes it friendly to newer leaders and groups mixing abilities. The route names follow a dental theme, and the left side of the cliff is where people set up belays and anchor access.

ut_8_mile_area.blurb: The 8 Mile Area is a modest bouldering pocket in the Left Fork of Joe's Valley, central Utah, found on sandstone beside the canyon road. It has 16 recorded problems spread evenly from VB-level up to V10, so there is something for most abilities, though the best-known lines are in the V4 to V9 range. A couple of the standout boulders can be seen from the road, a short scramble uphill. There is no built trail, so you pick your own way across the sandy ground.

ut_walls_of_liberation.blurb: Walls of Liberation is a sport crag on the north side of the Right Fork of Maple Canyon, in central Utah. It has 16 bolted routes, mostly from 5.6 to 5.10 with a lone 5.11, so the moderate grades dominate and it suits climbers wanting something between the busiest walls. The wall is shaded in the morning. Many lines have seen little traffic, so expect some dirt and loose rock, particularly on the less-travelled routes.

ut_white_harlem.blurb: White Harlem is a ridgetop bouldering zone in the Swett Hills near Cedar City, in southwest Utah, perched above the main wash and the last part of the Swett Hills to be developed. It offers 16 problems from VB through V9, with most of them at V2 to V5 and a few hard ones at the top. Views from up on the ridge are good. The boulders are spread out, but the trails between them are decent, and the zone catches morning sun before shade arrives in the afternoon.
